udl.lead: Practical ways to open the example Critical Thinking Online Breakout to every learner, organized by the three principles of the CAST Universal Design for Learning Guidelines (version 3.0). The breakout already builds in many of these supports across all seven languages.

elps.lead: How to use the example breakout with emergent bilingual students, aligned to the Texas English Language Proficiency Standards across listening, speaking, reading, and writing.

guide.lead: A ready structure for building a lesson around the example Critical Thinking Online Breakout, following a standard Texas lesson-plan format. A worked example appears at the end.
guide.ex.name: Round and Round: The Water Cycle
guide.ex.bigidea: Water moves continuously through evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection in a repeating cycle.
guide.ex.eq: How does water move from the ocean, into the sky, and back again?
guide.ex.obj: Students will sequence the steps of the water cycle and explain what drives each step, using evidence.
guide.ex.vocab: evaporation, condensation, precipitation, collection, water vapor
